title: Angry user raising their voice
symptom: User is shouting about a recurring problem
user_description: This is the THIRD time this week! You people never fix anything! I've got a client waiting and nothing works!

options.text: Raise your voice to match so he takes you seriously
options.why: Escalates the situation and makes you look unprofessional.

options.text: Tell him to calm down and wait his turn
options.why: Dismissive. Telling an upset person to calm down usually makes them angrier.

options.text: Stay calm, listen, acknowledge his frustration, apologise for the inconvenience, and explain what you will do next and when
options.why: People calm down when they feel heard. A clear next step with a timeframe shows you are taking it seriously.

hints: What does an angry person need first, solutions or being heard?
How should your voice and words sound?
real_world_tip: Don't take it personally. The anger is about the problem, not about you.
